aria: Animated recap of the Grizzlies' 124 to 121 win at Cleveland: Cameron Boozer's two go-ahead free throws with 1:26 left, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Cam Spencer's 26 points on 9-of-11 shooting, the top scorers, how Memphis won, and Thursday's game against Golden State.
notes: Box score from the Memphis Grizzlies' 124–121 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena on Nov 18, 2026, from the FantasyTeamAdvice box score, checked against the StatMuse game page, with team stats from theScore and Grizzlies On SI and game details from the Associated Press (via Cleveland 19), cleveland.com, Fear The Sword and Yardbarker. All 124 Memphis points and all 121 Cleveland points are accounted for, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Cleveland 37–30 after one, 72–71 at the half, Memphis 100–99 after three. The two box scores split one pair of free throws differently: FantasyTeamAdvice has Taylor Hendricks with 20 points (7 of 8 free throws) and Cedric Coward with 18; StatMuse has Hendricks 18 and Coward 20. The AP story and Grizzlies On SI both give Hendricks 20 and Coward 18, so those are used. Field goals (42 of 78 to 44 of 95), threes (16 of 39 to 15 of 41), free throws (24 of 29 to 18 of 20) and assists (30–28) are from the box score; offensive rebounds (5–20) from theScore; fast-break points (19–11) and points in the paint (48–56) from Grizzlies On SI. Cleveland's biggest lead (10) is from Yardbarker; no source gave Memphis' biggest lead, so it is left off. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Wednesday's games.

There were 22 lead changes, eight of them in the fourth quarter (AP). Cam Spencer made his first nine shots (AP). Donovan Mitchell's layup put Cleveland up 119–116 with 2:43 left (AP); Cleveland led by one at the two-minute mark (cleveland.com) and Boozer's two free throws with 1:26 left made it 120–119 (AP; Yardbarker). Memphis was called for a five-second inbounds violation with 15.9 seconds left, up 122–121 (AP; cleveland.com), and Sam Merrill, a career 89% free-throw shooter (cleveland.com), missed two with 6.6 seconds left (AP). Memphis' two free throws with 2.3 seconds left made it 124–121 (AP). It was a franchise-record eighth straight road win (AP). Ty Jerome (hip) was out for Memphis and Evan Mobley (toe) for Cleveland (AP; Yardbarker). Memphis hosts Golden State on Thursday (Yardbarker).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Cameron Boozer's two free throws with 1:26 left that put Memphis ahead 120–119 for good (AP; Yardbarker). It is drawn as one shot from the free-throw line. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Memphis Grizzlies or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Boozer's measurements at the 2026 NBA Draft Combine, 6-foot-8¼ and 253 pounds with a 7-foot-1½ wingspan (NBADraft.net), in Memphis' road colors with No. 27 (RealGM). He has no approved look on file yet, so he is drawn in the kit with the default skin tone. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
